html:
The Palatinate is a region on the west bank of the Rhine in southwestern Germany. After 1815 it was handed to the Kingdom of Bavaria as its Rhenish Palatinate, and it stayed Bavarian until 1946.

Its name comes from the Electoral Palatinate, whose counts palatine were among the seven electors of the Holy Roman Empire, with their seat at Heidelberg. The region was wrecked in the Thirty Years' War and again by French armies in the 1680s and 1690s. Many of its people emigrated, and "Palatines" became a common name for German settlers in America.

France annexed the left bank in the 1790s, and the French legal code stayed in force after 1815. The region kept a liberal streak: in 1832 the Hambach Festival gathered thousands for German unity and freedom. Cut off from the rest of Bavaria, it was joined in 1946 to the new state of Rhineland-Palatinate.
sum: The Palatinate is a region on the west bank of the Rhine in southwestern Germany. After 1815 it was handed to the Kingdom of Bavaria as its Rhenish Palatinate, and it stayed Bavarian until 1946.
